subject: Clarification on reserved GPU throughput windows and queueing behavior (SynapseCap)
messages:
From: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@synapsecap.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procurement <procurement@synapsecap.com>, Rajiv Narayan <rajiv@synapsecap.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved GPU throughput during scheduled batch windows — clarification request

Hi Hannah,

Quick question from our ops team: we run a nightly 3-hour batch (00:00–03:00 UTC) that needs predictable throughput. In the contract excerpt you shared (attached), “Reserved Throughput” is defined in tokens/sec and tied to reserved GPUs, but the scheduling appendix allows for routine maintenance windows and preemption for high-priority infra tasks.

Can you confirm: during a maintenance or preemption event, are we allowed to schedule our batch to still consume the full reserved throughput (i.e., are those GPUs logically reserved for our use and isolated from preemption), or will queueing/backpressure apply and we may see throughput drop? We need to know whether to shift windows or request an SLA carveout.

Thanks — appreciate a short, definitive answer.

Aisha Malik
Head of Platform Engineering
SynapseCap

---

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@synapsecap.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU throughput during scheduled batch windows — clarification request

Aisha,

Thanks for the clear question. Short answer: reserved GPUs give you priority on the nodes in your pool but do not absolutely exempt workload from maintenance-preemptions or system-level balancing. We should be explicit about two separate guarantees in the contract:

- Capacity reservation (nodes/GPU count): we guarantee access to a set of GPUs dedicated to your account within the reserved pool.
- Throughput SLO (tokens/sec or RPS): we guarantee steady-state throughput under normal operating conditions; however, the SLO includes exceptions for "unplanned maintenance, security patches, and critical infrastructure events".

What that means in practice: routine, scheduled maintenance windows are planned and we try to avoid them during customer-defined critical windows; if a scheduled maintenance overlaps, we surface advance notice and offer options (reschedule maintenance, temporary burst credits, or a compensatory credit if the scheduled maintenance was Redwood-initiated outside agreed windows). For preemption caused by emergency infra work, there may be transient queueing until workloads are migrated.

That said, for your nightly batch use-case we can offer an explicit scheduling carveout in the Reserved Capacity Addendum: a limited number of hours where maintenance-preemption is suppressed for your pool, or we can guarantee a minimum inflight concurrency and token-rate during your window with an associated price uplift. I’m looping in Ben and David to propose concrete options.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

---

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@synapsecap.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 08:29:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU throughput during scheduled batch windows — clarification request

Hi Aisha — hi team,

Following up with concrete proposal and the tradeoffs so SynapseCap can pick what fits ops and procurement:

Option A — Scheduling Carveout (recommended for reliability):
- We designate a 3-hour protected window per UTC day (00:00–03:00 UTC as requested).
- During that window we suppress planned maintenance and lower-priority preemption for your reserved pool.
- We guarantee minimum inflight concurrency (X concurrent generators per GPU) and minimum token-rate of Y tokens/sec per GPU.
- Pricing: +12% on the reserved capacity monthly fee or a fixed monthly add-on.
- Notes: emergency security patches still get an exception path (with 48-hour notice where possible) into the playbook.

Option B — Throughput SLO + Credit Backstop (no scheduling carveout):
- No change to maintenance scheduling; your workload remains priority on reserved GPUs during normal ops.
- If throughput falls below the guaranteed token-rate for more than the agreed tolerance window (e.g., 5% of scheduled window across a month), we issue service credits (pro-rated) and prioritize remediation.
- Pricing: no uplift but tighter contract definitions and observability hooks (per-route token/latency metrics).

Option C — Hybrid (preferred for price-sensitive customers):
- We provide a smaller protected window (1 hour/day) plus a lower guaranteed token-rate during adjacent hours.
- Pricing: +6% uplift.

Operational details we need from SynapseCap to finalize:
1) Confirm the exact UTC window(s) and whether they are fixed weekdays or calendar days.
2) Expected steady-state token/sec and peak concurrency during the window (approx numbers are fine).
3) Whether SynapseCap can accept an exception path for emergency security maintenance with X hours notice.

I’m attaching a short excerpt from the SLA and a sample amendment draft. Lauren — if procurement/legal at SynapseCap is comfortable with the sample language, we can convert it to a formal addendum and route for signature (DocuSign link included).

Happy to set up a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the schedule and pricing.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Dedicated Products
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-sla-excerpt.pdf
Attachment: synapsecap_mrp_schedule.csv

---

From: procurement <procurement@synapsecap.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU throughput during scheduled batch windows — clarification request

Thanks — this is helpful. We reviewed Options A–C with ops and finance. SynapseCap prefers Option C (hybrid) given cost constraints, but we need the following to move forward:

- Confirm the hybrid token-rate guarantee in plain numbers (tokens/sec per GPU) so our SREs can validate against existing job profiles.
- Add a clause that scheduled maintenance cannot be moved into our protected 1-hour window without mutual agreement (we can accept emergency exceptions with 24-hour notice where possible).
- Include an explicit runbook for rollover: if a maintenance event intrudes, Redwood will attempt live-migration with less than 10 minutes of degraded throughput; if migration cannot complete, Redwood issues a credit per the SLO backstop.

If you can incorporate those bullets into the addendum draft we’ll circulate to legal and sign. We’re OK with the +6% uplift.

Next steps: Ben/Hannah — please update the draft and share a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Regards,
SynapseCap Procurement Team
procurement@synapsecap.com
